no_new_call_note: The live register is still empty, so there was nothing to review or post-mortem this week. On the hunt itself: the Middle East conflict's spillover - oil above $100 a barrel, US diesel crack spreads above $106, and supertanker rates near $800,000 a day on the Hormuz-to-China route - are each already the lead story on Bloomberg, Reuters and the general wires as of September 10-11, not ahead of where attention sits. South Korea's record August semiconductor exports, up 209% year on year, were already written into the same week's mainstream market updates. The Senate's procedural vote on the CLARITY Act, dated for September 15, has been reported and anticipated by legal and financial press for weeks - a calendar event the market already expects, not a variant against it. China's rare-earth export-control suspension is set to expire November 10, but that date has been public since the suspension was announced and nothing new happened this week to change the thesis. The gap between the uranium term price (near $96/lb) and lagging junior-miner equities is real but has been argued repeatedly in specialist mining press across write-ups stretching back to the second quarter - a running narrative, not a fresh dated development. Nothing found this week was simultaneously new, confirmed by more than one independent source, and still ahead of where the market's attention already sits - so no call was opened. An empty week is counted, not apologized for.
